title: Dark Energy and Dark Matter as Cosmological Manifestations of Quantum-Cosmological Emergence Constraints— A Unified Framework of Quantum Entropy–Enthalpy Competition, ETH Saturation, and Cosmic Acceleration
content: This paper is a cosmological extension of our series of works on ``spacetime emergence'' and the ``entropy-driven Dirac equation.'' Starting from the entropy current vector \(s^\mu\) and the generalized second law \(\nabla_\mu s^\mu = \sigma \ge 0\) constructed in the previous two works, we treat the universe as a whole quantum object and study the evolution of its cosmic entropy-enthalpy ratio \(X_{\cos} = \ln(s_{\cos}/(k_B H_{\cos}))\). The core physical picture is as follows: after the quantum superfluid phase transition, classical spacetime structure and horizon entropy emerge simultaneously; dark energy, as the quantum ground state remaining after the phase transition, has zero thermodynamic entropy and does not contribute to the cosmic volume entropy; the growth of the total cosmic entropy is dominated by the thermal entropy of visible matter and radiation and by horizon configuration entropy. In this picture, the cosmic entropy-enthalpy ratio is not monotonic over cosmic history, but reaches a peak at the epoch when dark energy begins to dominate cosmic expansion, with a corresponding redshift \(z_{\text{peak}} \sim 0.3-0.5\), and then approaches the ETH saturation value from above. This non-monotonic evolution naturally explains the phantom crossing hinted at by DESI DR2. We derive the phenomenological form of the dark-energy equation of state as \(w(z) = w_0 - \delta w \tanh((z-z_{\text{peak}})/z_*)\), with the theoretical prediction \(w_0 = -1\); the equivalent theoretical form is \(w(z) = -1 + \delta w \tanh((z_{\text{peak}}-z)/z_*)\). Dark matter is interpreted as enthalpy-driven topologically protected bound states, whose lifetime and scattering cross section satisfy exponential scaling laws. The coincidence problem \(\Omega_m/\Omega_\Lambda \sim \mathcal{O}(1)\) is explained as a natural consequence of the universe approaching the ETH saturation boundary. The ETRG parameter \(a_{\text{ETRG}}\), determined by the contraction factor of the equivalent tensor renormalization group flow, lies in the conservative range \(0.7-0.9\). We explicitly list two falsifiable conditions.
